notes.summary: Partial P02.1: over every complete nontrivially valued field, the specified Gauss boundary jump on a strict n-polydisc (n>=2) has local continuous sequential approximation iff the residue field is countable. Explicit decreasing semipositive real-PL nets always exist; this is not a net obstruction or an all-functions classification.
notes.detailedSummary: The Laurent-field/coefficient-field/algebraic-closedness/discreteness assumptions in the supplied example are unnecessary. Lift all monic irreducible residue polynomials to monic integral polynomials. They detect every non-Gauss point by an attained-norm reduction argument valid also for nondiscrete valuations. With c=-log|a|>0, V_(F,m)=c^(-1) log max(1,|a^(-1)P_F^m|) is semipositive strict real-PL and decreases to the Gauss indicator; substitute T_1 for a genuine higher-dimensional example. Countable residue gives an explicitly cofinal sequence, without a countable dense field assumption. Uncountable residue gives cofinite families of lifted residue points in every Gauss neighborhood and excludes even nonmonotone continuous pointwise sequences. Classical curve-test admissibility includes every scalar extension, proved through analytic log/max laws and a harmonic-comparison decreasing-limit argument. The failure point is in the actual relative boundary. This criterion is exact only for this function and does not solve P02.1.
notes.text:
This is a partial mathematical draft, not an independent correctness verdict. Let K be any complete nontrivially valued non-Archimedean field, k its residue field, a in K with 0<|a|<1, and c=-log|a|. Put D=M(K<T>), X_n=M(K<T_1,...,T_n>) for n>=2. Let eta be the Gauss point, p the first-coordinate projection, and i:D->X_n the analytic section with the other coordinates zero. Define w=1_{eta}, u=w o p and x=i(eta). These are actual good strict affinoid spaces, separated and of the standard Tate-algebra dimensions 1 and n. Claim: u is finite bounded usc and classical psh, x is in the relative boundary, and u has local pointwise continuous sequential approximation near x iff k is countable. In the countable case a decreasing finite semipositive real-PL sequence works on all of X_n. For every k there is a decreasing semipositive real-PL net on all of X_n.

Definitions and primary inputs. Classical psh is the upper semicontinuous scalar-extension curve-test definition in Gubler--Rabinoff, Classically psh and pluriharmonic functions on Berkovich spaces, arXiv:2506.13548v2 (17 September 2025), Definition 4.1. The curve class in Definition 3.4 permits the identically -infinity function and tests smooth connected strict curves over every nontrivially valued analytic extension; Section 4.1.3 allows these smooth tests for the classical class. Proposition 4.2(2),(3) supplies analytic logarithms, finite maxima, and nonnegative linear combinations; (4) supplies decreasing-net closure. Theorem 4.3 states exactly that, over a nontrivially valued complete field, an already real-valued real-PL function on a good strictly analytic space is semipositive iff it is classical psh. No separatedness, pure-dimensionality or boundaryless qualification is added. Semipositivity here is geometric: the residue line bundle on the reduction of the germ is nef, meaning nonnegative degrees on integral proper residue curves on a finite-type model. Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff, Forms on Berkovich spaces based on harmonic tropicalizations, arXiv:2111.05741v3, Definition 5.1, Proposition 7.1 and Definition 7.2 give strict PL and residue/formal-model nefness, not an approximation-based definition.

The immediate primary statements/proofs were read and their bibliographic versions authenticated. The proof of GR Theorem 4.3 invokes the distinct March paper On semipositive piecewise linear functions in non-archimedean analytic geometry, arXiv:2503.05513v1, whose actual curve comparison and smooth-curve recognition are Proposition 5.1 and Corollary 5.4. June cites earlier labels 3.1/3.5; no theorem was inferred solely from that mismatch. The March proof passes residue-nef degrees to curves using the local lifting theorem and proper-surjective semipositivity descent. Deeper imported foundations include Thuillier harmonic comparison/Poincare--Lelong, Wanner's PL/current comparison inside the March proof, formal-model existence, Temkin reductions, degree projection formulas, and standard affinoid/Tate theory. No fresh recursive proof of all of them is claimed. No book theorem or historical PASS receipt is a premise.

Legal truncation lemma. For any analytic f on a good strict space and b in K*, H=log max(|b|,|f|) is finite integral PL and semipositive. On every strict affinoid neighborhood, the strict Laurent domains |f|<=|b| and |f|>=|b| form a finite G-cover. Their expressions are log|b| and log|f| respectively. On the second domain f is a unit, with inverse furnished by adjoining b/f. The expressions agree on the intersection, so they give one continuous integral PL function. The cut is an actual field value, preserving strictness. Analytic log/max laws make H classical psh, so the already-real-PL comparison proves residue-nef semipositivity. Positive real multiples and finite positive real sums remain real-PL by common refinement of their strict covers and are semipositive by the same cone/comparison argument. We do not assume closure under maxima of arbitrary real-PL functions, which can fail in the strict topology (GJR Example 5.3).

Decreasing-limit justification for these finite approximants. The infimum of finite continuous decreasing classical psh functions is usc: its strict sublevels are unions of the approximants' open strict sublevels. After any analytic extension and pullback to a smooth connected strict test curve, call the finite subharmonic functions g_i and their infimum g. If g is identically -infinity it is admissible. Otherwise take a strictly affinoid test domain A and a harmonic H on A with g<=H on its finite boundary. For each epsilon>0 choose an index at each boundary point with g_i<H+epsilon. A directed upper bound for those finitely many indices gives one function dominated by H+epsilon on the whole boundary. Harmonic comparison gives domination throughout A. Take the infimum and then epsilon to zero. This proves the required subharmonic test including negative-infinite values, and agrees with GR Proposition 4.2(4). Thus no current recognition is substituted for classical admissibility.

Detection lemma. Let R be the set of monic irreducibles q in k[T], and choose a monic coefficient lift Q_q in K^circ[T]. Every y!=eta has |Q_q(y)|<1 for some q. Indeed, a nonzero Tate series f has attained Gauss norm in |K*|, since its coefficients tend to zero. Dividing by an attaining coefficient gives norm one and nonzero polynomial reduction. Reduction of products proves multiplicativity of the Gauss norm. Every bounded multiplicative seminorm is bounded by this norm: apply its boundedness inequality to f^N and take Nth roots. Distinctness from eta gives f with |f(y)|<||f||. Normalize and factor its reduction as dbar times product q_r^{e_r}. Lift dbar to a unit d and put R_f=d product Q_(q_r)^{e_r}. Then ||f-R_f||<1. This strict inequality needs no discreteness: the difference coefficients all have norm less than one and tend to zero, so their attained maximum is less than one. Hence |R_f(y)|<1. All factors are at most one and d has norm one, so some factor is less than one. A constant nonzero reduction cannot occur in this situation. This proves detection without a coefficient subfield or algebraic closure.

Net. Direct Fin(R) x N_(>=1) by inclusion and integer order. Set P_F=product_(q in F)Q_q, P_empty=1, and V_(F,m)=c^(-1)log max(1,|a^(-1)P_F^m|)=max(0,1+(m/c)log|P_F|). At zeros use the first finite formula. The legal truncation lemma and positive scalar 1/c prove semipositive strict real-PL membership. The last identity is numerical, not an arbitrary-real-max membership assertion. Each factor has norm <=1, so increasing either index decreases V. At eta every monic product has norm one, giving value 1. Off eta a detecting factor of norm r<1 makes every index containing it bounded above by max(0,1+(m/c)log r), eventually zero. If r=0 it is zero immediately. Thus V decreases to w. Substituting T_1 gives one global net on X_n decreasing to u. The decreasing-limit argument proves w and u classical psh with every scalar curve test.

Boundary. The Gauss singleton is closed and attains every analytic norm, hence is the Shilov boundary. GR-C Section 3.1(3) identifies it with the relative boundary of the affinoid curve D. The boundary composition rule in Section 2.11(4') is equality for X_n->D->M(K), because D's structural map is separated. It implies p^(-1)(eta) is contained in the actual relative boundary of X_n. This proves x is a relative-boundary point, while the indicator formula proves usc directly as well.

Countable case. k[T] and R are countable when k is countable. R is infinite by the usual product-plus-one argument. Enumerate it q_1,q_2,... and set F_j={q_1,...,q_j}, m_j=j. For every finite F and every m, all sufficiently large j contain F and satisfy j>=m. This is a proved cofinal sequence, so it has the same decreasing pointwise limit on the whole domain. No second countability or countable dense subset of K is assumed for this particular function.

Uncountable case. Choose one lift b_alpha in K^circ of each alpha in k and the rigid point z_alpha:T=b_alpha. Every neighborhood of eta contains all but finitely many z_alpha. For a nonzero normalized Tate series its reduction is a nonzero polynomial; except at its finite root set in k, evaluation at b_alpha has the same norm as at eta. A basic neighborhood imposes conditions on only finitely many evaluations, so only finitely many residue classes are exceptional. Suppose h_j are continuous on an ordinary neighborhood W of x and converge pointwise to u. On U=i^(-1)(W), continuity at eta supplies neighborhoods N_j with |h_j(i(y))-h_j(x)|<1/4. Countably many such neighborhoods miss only a countable union of finite sets of z_alpha. Choose a residue class outside that union. At the chosen point all inequalities hold, whereas h_j(x)->1 and h_j(i(z_alpha))->0. Contradiction. These two points are distinct by evaluation of T-b_alpha. Monotonicity was never used.

The same negative argument passes to any good strict higher-dimensional space with an analytic retract D->Y->D, by restriction through the section. The polydiscs are actual examples. Every constructed formula is global on one fixed domain and agrees on its strict-domain intersections. Over any analytic extension, the same K-defined formulas converge to the pullback indicator, by equality of analytic evaluations downstairs/upstairs; they do not automatically give the native upstairs Gauss indicator.

Limitations: this is an exact countability criterion for one function, not the original all-functions space characterization. The failure requires the displayed relative boundary. It is not a net obstruction: the explicit net always works. Countable residue is not asserted sufficient for every classical psh input. No other P02 atom is counted. Full proofs are embedded in P02.1-paper.tex and P02.1-whole-proof.md; source boundaries are in whole-source-application-ledger.md. Rerun the bounded artifact/evidence build with python programs/reproduce.py in this directory. The manuscript and all findings remain unverified drafts.

notes.summary: Partial P02.1 positive sector: on any good strict space over a complete nontrivially valued field, a negative series sum lambda_i log|f_i| of bounded analytic functions has an explicit decreasing semipositive real-PL sequence, including -infinity and noninvariant poles. The analytic-series representation is an extra hypothesis; arbitrary classical psh germs are not covered.
notes.detailedSummary: For |f_i|<=1 and positive real lambda_i, with no summability assumption, u_j=sum_(i<=j) lambda_i log max(|a|^j,|f_i|) is finite semipositive strict real-PL by the integral truncation lemma in n1. Lowering thresholds and adding a nonpositive term proves monotonicity. u_j>=u; for fixed N and j>=N the first N truncated terms bound u_j above and converge to the N-term series. Taking the infimum in N gives the exact pointwise limit, including -infinity. The same formulas prove scalar/morphism compatibility and strict-domain overlap agreement on one fixed space; compact uniform convergence holds where the limit is finite continuous. An explicit Q_p bidisc example has countably many polar lines and is not invariant under a unit torus action. This is not an all-functions geometric regime or a full solution of P02.1.
notes.text:
Let K be complete and nontrivially valued and let X be any good strictly K-analytic space. Give analytic functions f_1,f_2,... on this one X, with |f_i|<=1 everywhere, and real lambda_i>0. Define u(y)=sum_i lambda_i log|f_i(y)| as the infimum of the nonpositive finite partial sums, with log 0=-infinity. This input definition uses analytic functions, not an approximation class. No continuity, finiteness or coefficient summability is assumed. Claim: u is classical psh and is the decreasing pointwise limit on all of X of finite semipositive real-PL functions u_j=sum_(i=1)^j lambda_i log max(|a|^j,|f_i|), where a is any fixed field element with 0<|a|<1. The target may be identically -infinity. Zero coefficients may be discarded to avoid undefined zero times negative infinity.

The complete strict integral truncation and classical decreasing-limit lemmas, with exact primary-source conditions, are proved in n1 and used here. In particular each max is an integral PL construction cut at an actual field value |a|^j; the real lambda_i are applied afterward. The approximant does not rely on arbitrary real-PL-max closure, an all-domain lisse identification, current recognition, or a smooth/FS comparison. Its semipositivity is geometric residue/model nefness, supplied after strict membership by the authenticated real-PL/classical comparison.

Proof. Every u_j is finite, continuous, nonpositive, and semipositive real-PL by finite common refinement of the truncation covers. All these terms have the same domain X. Raising j lowers the truncation threshold in every old summand and adds a nonpositive new term. Thus u_(j+1)<=u_j. Omitting a nonpositive tail and clipping old terms upward proves u_j>=u. Let ell=inf_j u_j. For every fixed N and j>=N, negativity of the omitted terms gives u_j<=sum_(i<=N) lambda_i log max(|a|^j,|f_i|). At a fixed point this finite sum decreases to sum_(i<=N) lambda_i log|f_i|. If any factor vanishes, both this limit and its extended sum are -infinity; positive lambda_i create no ambiguity. Therefore ell<=sum_(i<=N) lambda_i log|f_i| for every N. Taking the infimum in N yields ell<=u. Together with ell>=u this proves ell=u at every point, including all divergent and polar cases. The decreasing-limit argument of n1 verifies usc and all scalar curve tests, so u is classical psh.

Every strict-domain local expression is a restriction of the displayed global formula; on intersections the values agree term by term. Under an analytic morphism from a good strict source, or under any analytic field extension, evaluate the same pulled-back analytic functions. Their values and bounds are the downstairs values. The formula therefore commutes with pullback, remains finite semipositive strict real-PL by the same truncation argument, and decreases to the pulled-back series. This concerns pullbacks of the given data, not arbitrary new psh functions over an extension. There is no net extraction: the countable sequence is explicitly constructed from the given countable analytic input family.

If C is a compact subset on which u is finite and continuous, the increasing open subsets of C defined by u_j-u<epsilon cover C. Compactness supplies one index covering C. Hence convergence is uniform on C, without a metrizability assumption. For discontinuous or extended-valued limits only pointwise convergence is asserted.

Concrete noninvariant polar example. Over K=Q_p take the actual strict bidisc, f_1=T_1-T_2, f_i=T_1-p^(i-1)T_2 for i>=2, and lambda_i=2^(-i). Each function has norm at most one on the entire bidisc. At its Gauss point all f_i have norm one, giving u=0. At (1,1), f_1 vanishes and u=-infinity. At (1+p,1), f_1 has norm |p| and all later f_i are units of norm one, giving u=(1/2)log|p|. Multiplication of the first coordinate by the unit 1+p sends the first point to the second, so the function is not invariant under the maximal compact torus. Every polar line f_i=0 is included in the domain. The displayed u_j approximates all of it, including its relative boundary and extended poles.

This proves a sufficient starting-function sector on a geometrically unrestricted good strict X, not a sufficient all-functions regime for arbitrary higher-dimensional germs. No representation of an arbitrary classical psh function by this analytic series has been proved. The extra hypothesis is explicit and noncircular. The full P02.1 characterization remains unresolved, and no FS, weak-smooth or ordinary-smooth conclusion is inferred. Full proof and source conditions are in P02.1-whole-proof.md and its standalone P02.1-paper.tex embedding. Rerun python programs/reproduce.py. This note is an unverified draft and relies only on earlier own note n1, not supplied historical notes.

notes.summary: Scalar-extension distinction and delivery: an explicit Gauss-valued extension of Q_p changes the native boundary-jump sequence criterion while preserving a sequence for the pulled-back original function. The eight-page standalone paper, full-proof companion, source/scope/coverage ledgers and bounded checks are delivered. Full P02.1 remains unresolved; candidate=false.
notes.detailedSummary: Complete the Gauss-valued rational function field Q_p(t_alpha) for uncountably many independent variables. Polynomial reduction proves a valued-field extension whose completion has uncountable residue field F_p(t_alpha). n1 gives sequential regularization for the Q_p-native jump and its pullback, but no continuous sequence for the new native jump. The point T=t_alpha maps to eta_Qp, so the two upstairs functions actually differ. All 46 manifest-bound files match their lengths and hashes; four fresh PDF-to-text extractions are byte-identical to retained text; the rational diagnostics exhaust 125 three-term series cases and 1701 comparable pairs in a 96-index net proxy. Pandoc and both TeX passes succeed, yielding an eight-page PDF with no final box/warning diagnostics. These are execution observations, not mathematical certificates. Whole unused book/private-primary physical reading and deeper recursive foundation verification are not claimed. The positive analytic-series theorem has an extra input hypothesis, and the negative boundary example admits nets, so the original characterization is not resolved.
notes.text:
Scalar-extension claim. For any analytic extension L/K, the n1 net, and when available its sequence, formed with the original K-defined polynomials converges to w_K o pi on D_L, by the literal norm identity for analytic evaluation. Its support is pi^(-1)(eta_K), not necessarily the singleton eta_L. n2 similarly preserves the series sequence for the original analytic data. This is a pointwise pullback statement on a fixed domain with exact agreement of its formulas on all strict-domain overlaps. It is not a theorem about every new classical psh function over L.

An explicit field proof makes the distinction concrete. Take K=Q_p, an uncountable index set A, and F=Q_p(t_alpha:alpha in A). On a polynomial give the norm by the maximum norm of its finitely many coefficients, equivalently the p-adic valuation is the minimum coefficient valuation. After scalar normalization, nonzero polynomial reductions have nonzero product in the domain F_p[t_alpha]. Thus the Gauss norm is multiplicative and extends consistently to fractions. It gives a valued field extending Q_p. Only finitely many variables occur in each polynomial. Its residue field is F_p(t_alpha:alpha in A): a unit fraction has equal numerator and denominator valuations, so after cancelling their common scalar its residue is the quotient of their nonzero reductions; every such residue fraction lifts. Elements of positive valuation reduce to zero. Let L be the completion. It has the same residue field, because every integral element of L is within distance less than one of an element of F, which is then integral with the same residue. Thus L is complete and nontrivially valued, with uncountable residue field, while K has finite residue field.

By n1 the native jump on D_K has a decreasing semipositive real-PL sequence, and its literal scalar pullback has the same sequence on D_L. The native jump w_L=1_{eta_L} has no continuous pointwise approximating sequence near eta_L, again by n1. For a fixed alpha, the L-rational point T=t_alpha maps to eta_K. To prove this directly, normalize any nonzero K-Tate series to norm one; its nonzero polynomial reduction lies in F_p[T], and evaluation at the transcendental residue of t_alpha is nonzero. Hence its value at that point is its Gauss norm. Equality for all analytic evaluations identifies its image as eta_K. Therefore (w_K o pi)(t_alpha)=1, whereas w_L(t_alpha)=0. The example does not claim the full all-functions P02.1 property over Q_p; it only distinguishes these two functions and the exact single-function criterion of n1. Substitution of T_1 gives the same phenomenon on actual higher-dimensional strict polydiscs.

Source-reading and acceptance limits. The two historical whole manuscript/argument pairs and all distinct historical mathematical note bodies were reconstructed as data, including the complete final-note variant and the independent-review limitations. The old projective-bundle result needs entire proper fibres, the old boundary result excludes sequences but admits nets, and weakly smooth is not ordinary CLD-smooth. Wu Definition 3.8 specifies an approximation-generated local class on opens of projective analytifications; that definition alone is not the missing bridge for every extended classical curve-test psh function.

The full original P02.1 target remains unresolved by this work. n1 gives an actual relative-boundary sequence failure and an exact threshold only for that jump; its explicit nets rule out calling it a net obstruction. n2 gives a noninvariant extended-pole input sector, with an analytic-series representation not proved for arbitrary classical functions. There is no noncircular geometric characterization for every classical psh germ, no boundaryless higher-dimensional classification, no general singular normalization descent, and no arbitrary-chart construction/extraction/gluing theorem. These limitations are retained in the full paper. The implementation deliverable is complete as partial research, while candidate=false and no original target or other atom is counted solved.
